actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.name: seed

facts.text: The repository describes itself as a reinforcement learning workspace for CoppeliaSim (VREP) simulation environments
The environment setup lists CoppeliaSim 4.2 and the legacy Gym package as required software
The cart-pole demo is started after CoppeliaSim is running and cart_pole.ttt has been imported
CartPoleEnv is a gym.Env subclass
The constructor builds a Discrete(3) action space when action_type is 'discrete' and a Box(-1.0, 1.0) action space when it is 'continuous'
The cart-pole demo instantiates CartPoleEnv with action_type='discrete'
In the discrete action mapping action 0 applies zero force, action 1 applies +1.0 and action 2 applies -1.0
For a continuous action the push force is action*2.0, so the action range -1.0 to 1.0 maps to -2.0 to 2.0
The failure thresholds are a cart position of 0.8 and a pole angle of 40*pi/360 rad
The episode ends when the cart position reaches +-0.8 or the pole angle leaves +-40*pi/360 rad
The observation is [cart position, pole angle, cart linear velocity, pole angular velocity]
Joint velocities are computed by dividing the position change by a 0.005 s interval
A reset draws the four state values uniformly from -0.05 to 0.05
Every step that is not done pays reward 1.0; the first step after done pays 1.0 and later steps pay 0.0
The reset stops and restarts the CoppeliaSim simulation and sets the joint torque to zero
The environment connects to the remote API server at 127.0.0.1 on port 19997 and runs it in synchronous mode
Each step triggers one synchronous simulation advance and waits for its ping time
The joint driver sets the prismatic joint target velocity to +-1000 and its maximum force to abs(torque)
Joint positions are read from the prismatic and revolute joints through the remote API buffer mode
The remote API wrapper loads a platform-specific remoteApi library (remoteApi.so, .dll or .dylib) next to sim.py
CartPoleEnv.close stops the simulation and finishes all remote API connections

determinism.notes: the environment seeds a numpy generator and draws the start state from it; the fake uses Python's random.Random, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two, and the CoppeliaSim scene itself was never run here

gaps: the physics lives in the binary cart_pole.ttt scene and the CoppeliaSim engine: mass, inertia, friction, contact and actuator parameters are not stated in the clone and were not read
the remote API sets a prismatic target velocity and a maximum force (CartPole/CartPoleSimModel.py:57-63); the resulting actuator dynamics, contacts and friction are not modelled by this package
the scene's actual simulation step is not stated in the clone: 5 ms is the interval the upstream velocity computation assumes (CartPole/CartPoleEnv.py:119-120), not a scene setting read here
the fake backend replaces the engine with placeholder displacement constants and was never compared with a running CoppeliaSim; its initial draw uses Python's random.Random, not numpy's generator
the upstream reset draws a start state but does not push it into the simulation; the fake keeps the drawn cart and pole positions as its own state
the fake advances the positions before returning them, while upstream reads the joints before it triggers the next synchronous step, so the reported state lags the applied action by one tick
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
